DUBAI — The Gulf Bar Show (GBS) confirmed new dates for its second edition: It will take place November 30-December 1, 2026, at the Madinat Jumeirah Conference & Events Centre.
p
GBS 2026 was originally scheduled for March 30-31, but was delayed due to the U.S. war with Iran.
p
While initially expected to double in size when compared to its debut, the show now expects to be similar in size to its first edition, which was a deliberate choice in a year like this.
p

“We started GBS in 2025 because the region had no dedicated trade show for the bar and beverage industry — no single place where the community could come together,” Hugo Goncalves, Co-Founder of GBS, said. “The first edition proved the need: 115 exhibitors, 208 brands and over 3,000 trade visitors. This year, the geopolitical situation in the region changed, and international guests weren’t comfortable traveling. Rather than run a weaker show, we moved it.”
p
The show’s team kept constant communication with its exhibitors, partners and the industry itself.
p

“It was a difficult period with a lot of unknowns, but we managed to navigate it together,” Goncalves said. “We asked our exhibitors, distributors and hospitality partners when they could realistically commit. Late November is peak season in Dubai; the city is full, and the trade is here. It was the natural moment.”
p

Running from 12:00 p.m. to 9:00 p.m., the region’s first and only dedicated bar and beverage trade show will bring together the bar industry and community across MENA for two days of talks, tastings and trade.
p
Related. The Gulf Bar Show — Billed as MENA’s First Bar and Beverage Trade Show — to Launch in 2025
p

GBS 2026 expects to welcome more than 3,000 industry leaders and professionals, and more than 100 global and regional exhibitors, alongside an educational program of more than 20 seminars and masterclasses, and more than 12 guided tasting sessions.
p

“We chose quality over size: the right exhibitors, the right buyers and better conversations. We also focused on a community-focused program, giving the region’s bartenders, bar teams and venues a bigger part in the show,” Goncalves said.
p
Its international speaker line-up includes Salvatore Calabrese, Ago Perrone, Ed Cottrell, Tristan Stephenson, Marcio Silva, Yuki Yamazaki and David Rios.
p

The panels cover vital issues for its industry, from retaining talent behind the bar to “Made in Dubai: The Women Shaping the Bar Scene.” Also, Tristan Stephenson will record The Curious Bartender podcast live across both days.
p
GBS is hosting “Bonded by Craft,” MENA’s first cocktail storytelling competition, with Jack Daniel’s Bonded Series, and visitors will vote for the winning team on December 1.
p

There will be guest shifts from some of the region’s best bars as well, including a Mimi Kakushi and Hope & Sesame collaboration, and four shifts on the GBS stand with the UAE bar community, and guided tastings with Bacardi, Brown-Forman, Sazerac, Fuji Whisky and more organizations.
p
This year, GBS will take place concurrently with Salon du Chocolat Dubai, creating a unique cross-industry experience.
p

“Relationships carry you. People stayed because they trusted us. Communicate early and honestly. The quality of the room matters more than its size,” Goncalves said, noting that 2027 is about consolidation, with the priority on rebooking and buyer quality. “We’re already confirmed for Q4 2027. We’re keeping the community engaged all year, not just for two days.”
p

For organizers who encounter extreme headwinds like the U.S.-Iran war, Goncalves had this advice: “Know who your show is for and let that guide every decision. Be straight with your exhibitors. Grow at a measured pace. Credibility is what brings people back. Thank you to the exhibitors, partners and the bar community who stood with us. GBS exists for the industry and its community. See you at Madinat Jumeirah on November 30 and December 1.”
